lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: Pay the fare, you little wretch.
lines.note: Flat, aggrieved. Not thunderous — this is a man chasing an invoice.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Shout if it makes you feel better, Charon.
lines.note: Perfectly pleasant. Not defiant — just unbothered.

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: Pay up, I said. For the crossing I gave you.
lines.note: He's repeating himself because nobody listens to him. He's used to this.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: You can't take something from someone who hasn't got it.
lines.note: Stated as a simple logical fact.

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: Is there anyone who hasn't got an obol?
lines.note: Genuine disbelief. In thirty thousand years of ferrying, this hasn't come up.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Whether anyone else hasn't, I couldn't say. I haven't.
lines.note: Helpful. Almost sympathetic.

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: I will strangle you, by Pluto I will, you filthy — if you don't pay.
lines.note: The threat is real but the delivery is exhausted. This is not his first difficult passenger today.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: And I'll crack your skull with your own oar.
lines.note: Still conversational. No raised voice.

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: So you'll have made the whole crossing for nothing.
lines.note: Sulking now. This is his actual grievance — the principle of the thing.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Have Hermes pay you. He's the one who handed me over.
lines.note: A genuinely reasonable suggestion, delivered as such.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Oh, excellent. Yes, I'll definitely be subsidising the dead out of my own pocket. That's exactly what I need.
lines.note: Dry. He is not angry — he is an overworked bureaucrat who has heard worse proposals.

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: I'm not letting this drop.
lines.note: Dug in.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Then haul the boat ashore and wait. [pause] But the thing I don't have — how are you going to get it?
lines.note: The pause is genuine: he's offering a practical suggestion before returning to the unanswerable logic.

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: You didn't know you were supposed to bring the fare?
lines.note: Looking for a technicality.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: I knew. I didn't have it. So what — should I have not died on that account?
lines.note: Perfectly sincere. The logic is airtight and Menippus knows it.

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: So you'll be the only one who gets to boast he crossed for free.
lines.note: This is the real wound: the precedent.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Not exactly free, my friend. I bailed water. I took a turn on the oar. And I was the only passenger who didn't cry.
lines.note: He's itemising his contribution with genuine seriousness. This is his fare.

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: That's got nothing to do with anything. The obol gets paid. That's the rule. There are no exceptions.
lines.note: The rules are the rules. He has retreated entirely into procedure.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Then send me back to the living.
lines.note: A perfectly logical counter-offer.

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: Oh, very funny. And then Aeacus gives me a beating on top of everything else. Wonderful.
lines.note: He knows this is absurd. He's just registering what his life is like.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Then stop bothering me.
lines.note: Final. Cheerful.

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: Show me what's in the bag.
lines.note: Last resort: maybe there's something seizable.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Lupine beans, if you want them. And the leftovers from Hecate's supper.
lines.note: He opens the bag helpfully. It contains exactly what you'd expect a Cynic philosopher to carry.

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: Hermes — where in Hades did you find this one? What was he doing the entire crossing? Laughing at every other passenger, making jokes, singing — singing, while everyone else was weeping.
lines.note: Genuinely aggrieved, and also slightly impressed despite himself.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: You don't know who you just ferried, Charon. A completely free man. Doesn't care about anything. [pause] This is Menippus.
lines.note: Warm. He likes Menippus. The pause before the name is a small gift to the actor.

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: If I ever get my hands on you —
lines.note: He knows this is empty. He's saying it anyway.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: If you do, friend. [pause] But you won't get me twice.
lines.note: The first sentence concedes the hypothetical graciously. The second closes the door. Both delivered without malice.
